title: Micro OKR Stitchbook — Weekly Coda (Oliver Wren)
content:
Purpose: compact weekly log to stitch together small outcome bets (micro-OKRs), tempo commitments, and one-week experiments. Quick to scan; preserved as single-source-of-truth for personal followups.

This week (2024-11-04 -> 2024-11-10) snapshot:
- Focus theme: lower tail latency investigations + developer onboarding flow for streaming SDK
- Primary micro-OKR: surface 3 low-effort ops to save 10% of token cost on the most common dev playground prompt by end of week.
- Secondary micro-OKR: reduce first-time dev onboarding time from 25 -> 18 minutes (measurement: stopwatch on 5 new dev volunteers).

Metrics (signal, how I measure, current value, target):
- Playground token cost per session: sample avg across 30 sessions = 1,250 tokens -> target 1,125 (-10%). Measurement: daily bucketed cost logs.
- Cold-start tail latency p95 (local repro harness): 1,120ms -> target <900ms. Measurement: harness run x10, median of p95.
- Onboarding time (volunteer median): 25m -> target 18m. Measurement: observed runs with checklist.
- Weekly focus hours (blocked, deep work): 11h -> target 16h. Tracked via calendar tags.
- Habit score (5 items): 3/5 consistent.

Current experiments (quick serverable summaries):
1) Prefix KV cache warmup script (A/B): warmup top-5 prompts on container startup. Hypothesis: reduces first-3-request latency by 25%. Setup: staging infra hook + warmup lambda. Observed: first-3 p95 improved 18% in noisy runs. Next: adjust prefetch order by usage frequency.
2) Batching window tweak in playground: 30ms -> 18ms. Hypothesis: small windows improve tail for short sequences. Observed: average latency slightly up (noise), p95 down ~8%. Need longer sample.
3) Streamlined Quickstart notebook (3 steps -> 2 steps): measure onboarding time. First volunteer run shaved ~4m but missed step for tracing. Action: add tiny inline trace step that auto-runs.

Retro notes (what worked / what didn’t):
- Worked: rapid pairing with infra on warmup script; short syncs were high bandwidth.
- Didn’t: I over-optimized the measurement rig (spent ~3h building fancy dashboards) instead of running more volunteer sessions. Tradeoff: measurement signal vs. actionable runs.
- Blockers: limited staging slots for dedicated GPU nodes; queued runs caused delayed verification.

Decisions & actions (owned by me unless reassign):
- Short: push warmup order change and re-run 3-day harness (owner: Oliver) — due Fri EOD.
- Short: add inline trace cell to quickstart notebook and run 3 volunteer sessions (owner: Oliver) — due Wed.
- Medium: propose a small quota for one dedicated staging slot to SRE for the week of Nov 18 to complete full-scale regressions (owner: Oliver -> request to Priya SRE).
- Medium: write mini postmortem of dashboard time sink and distill into checklist: for future experiments, prefer N=5 quick trials to N=1 fancy trials. (owner: Oliver)

Micro-OKR mapping (why it matters):
- Cost savings (playground token cost): direct product metric for developer experience; 10% at scale reduces billing friction in trial clusters.
- Latency tail: core to demo quality; p95 improvements increase perceived responsiveness, helps PLG conversions.
- Onboarding: lower friction correlates with higher retention in the first 48 hours.

Quick day-by-day plan:
- Mon: pair with infra, run warmup script baseline, schedule volunteer sessions.
- Tue: iterate batching window experiments; run 10 quick harness runs.
- Wed: volunteer onboarding sessions (at least 3), finalize quickstart notebook edits.
- Thu: longer harness + cost-sample collection.
- Fri: consolidate results, prepare short summary for team sync.

Signals to watch (stop / continue rules):
- Stop experiment if it increases median latency >5% for sequences <64 tokens.
- Continue warmup script if p95 improves >12% across first-5 requests consistently.
- Stop dashboard build if >6 hours spent without additional volunteers tested.

Notes to self (scratch, informal):
- Don’t fall into the perfection trap on instrumentation; small repeated runs beat one big dashboard.
- Call out SRE latency impact separately from model-level moves so product team sees clear ownership.
- Remember to mention the demo quality improvement in next week’s CS sync (Marta asked for a short blurb).

Personal weekly reflection (meta):
- Energy: mid-week slump Wednesday afternoon. Mitigation: short walk + 90-minute focused block in the morning.
- Time allocation feels skewed to infra plumbing vs. user feedback. Plan: schedule a 60m block on Thursday explicitly for volunteer interviews.

Todo riff (scratch list - short):
- [ ] Run warmup order change and log results (Fri)
- [ ] Ship quickstart inline trace + run 3 volunteers (Wed)
- [ ] Draft short summary for team sync (~10 bullet points) (Fri)
- [ ] Ping Priya about staging quota (ASAP)
- [ ] Add one-line note in personal handbook about measurement-first rule

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is 10% token reduction realistic without changing model weights or pruning? Need cost projection.
- Which onboarding step regresses if we compress steps further? Need to watch error rate in step 2.
- Can we get a non-prod quota for a single dedicated slot temporarily? SRE policy research needed.

Archive / context links (quick):
- Slack thread: #devexp-streaming "warmup experiments" (ref: t12345)
summary: Compact, iterative weekly planner focused on small repeatable experiments to improve playground cost, tail latency, and onboarding time. Emphasizes quick volunteer runs, conservative stop rules, and minimizing over-investment in instrumentation.
